Importantly, after the added water gas-shift, acid gas removal, and methanation purification stages, we find in Table 21 that the produced gas is able to meet all of the specified purity requirements, namely on heating value and sulfur content. We note that the modeled concentration of H (3.1 – 3.3%) is close to an order of magnitude higher than what is 2 typically seen in pipelines today; however, there was precedent in the literature for testing mixtures up to 5% with no apparent negative consequences. 29 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nrel.gov/publications. 5 Critical Processes and Parameters Across the two studied HighRG and HighAlc scenarios, we find that feedstock costs contribute to ~98% of the total variable operating costs and nearly 40% of the total product cost, thus sourcing the lowest costs feedstocks should be one of the highest priorities. Another ~50% of the total product cost was attributed to the capital investment charges. A significant fraction of the capital (~50%) arose from the newly added Area 1100 equipment required to purify the RG product to meet natural gas pipeline specifications. Consequently, reactor and catalyst modifications that minimize the downstream separations demands of the RG should also be prioritized to minimize the impact of the capital charges. 6 Conclusions In this analysis two configurations of the West Biofuels mixed alcohol synthesis reactor were studied: one to maximize the production of mixed alcohols and one favoring the production of renewable gas. The economic analysis shows in the RG production configuration, RG can be produced with an estimated cost of $19.00 - $22.60 / MMBtu depending on whether a $40/tonne CO sequestration credit is claimed. This puts the estimated cost on the cusp of the upper 2 targeted range of $12-$21/MMBtu. In alcohol production configuration, estimated production cost of the targeted ethanol product ranged from $2.66 - $3.83 / gal EtOH depending on application of the same CO sequestration credit. This represents an increase in calculated cost 2 compared to the prior mixed alcohol reports published by NREL and West Biofuels that showed a production cost of approximately $2.20 / gal EtOH (in 2016$), without the RG production modifications and syngas conversion yield assumptions detailed in the design report [1]. Due to limitations in resources and data quality, these results should be viewed as high-level estimates only and more rigorous analyses using experimental data and measurements from the pilot-scale facility operating on forest residues should be performed for more accurate results. 30 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nrel.gov/publications.
